acceptance.statement: Infrastructure health uses a distinct authoritative non-trading schema and never requires or invents a RuntimeBinding. Every RuntimeBinding evidence field is refused at any depth by an unbounded, iterative ingest-path scan; metadata is deliberately additionalProperties true, so the scan rather than the schema is the enforcement point and the refusal must hold at depths no producer would reach.
Strict JWT service authentication plus tenant and producer scope is required for infrastructure ingestion and spoofed probe fields cannot bypass trading validation.

The admitted event is durable and idempotent by stable event ID across retries and replicas: admission fails closed unless the configured buffer is a durable broker, no caller is told it succeeded before a durable receipt exists, an admitted event survives process crash and restart, and four contending replica processes produce exactly one commit owner, one committed ledger receipt bound to that owner's token, and one durable broker copy.
Trading telemetry binding and lineage validation remains unchanged and fails closed.
Real strict-auth service tests cover valid ingest, missing token, wrong tenant, wrong producer, runtime-health spoof, restart, and duplicate replay.

proof: Admission is keyed by the producer's stable event_id and a sha256 fingerprint of the canonical event JSON in a two-phase append-only ledger under a POSIX advisory lock. Only a committed record — written after a durable enqueue receipt — makes an exact retry answer 202 duplicate; a caller that meets a live reservation is answered 503 INFRA_ADMISSION_IN_FLIGHT so it retries instead of treating an unpersisted observation as delivered.
Reusing an event_id for different content is refused with 409 INFRA_EVENT_ID_CONFLICT rather than silently overwriting the first observation.
Four concurrent replica processes racing on one event ID through a shared ledger produced exactly one committed receipt and three in-flight retry answers, and exactly one committed ledger record.

Under four contending replica processes over one ledger and one durable broker log, exactly one replica reaches the commit-owner role, the single committed ledger record carries that owner's token, and the durable log holds exactly one copy of the event. A replica that begins after the receipt is durable reads the same ledger word 'committed' as the owner's own commit, so it is classified by role rather than by that word and is counted as an idempotent duplicate, never as a second admission.

Missing bearer token, a structured permissive-mode token, the shared static service token, a non-service role, an unbound or wildcard tenant claim, a cross-tenant header, a payload tenant mismatch, an unconfigured or wildcard producer scope, and an unallowlisted producer all fail closed with stable error codes.

When the deployment has no durable broker behind the route, ingestion refuses the event with 503 INFRA_BUFFER_NOT_DURABLE before taking a reservation, rather than admitting an observation it cannot keep.

When the authoritative schema or the durable admission ledger is unavailable, ingestion refuses the event with INFRA_SCHEMA_UNAVAILABLE or INFRA_LEDGER_UNCONFIGURED instead of admitting something it cannot deduplicate.
A full buffer answers 503 INFRA_BUFFER_OVERFLOW, and a cancelled enqueue raises, with the ledger reservation released in both cases so the producer's retry can still be admitted.

A RuntimeBinding evidence field is refused wherever it appears, not only where a well-behaved producer would put it. The ingest-path scan is iterative with no depth ceiling, so a binding_id nested at depth 12 and a runtime_id at depth 40 through alternating lists and objects are both answered 400 INFRA_BINDING_FIELD_FORBIDDEN over real HTTP, while clean metadata nested 40 levels deep is still admitted with 202 — depth itself is not the gate. The scan also terminates on a self-referential payload without hiding a field. The previous revision capped recursion at depth 8 and returned no findings past it, which admitted the nested spoof.
HTTP 202 is returned only after the durable enqueue receipt exists and the reservation is committed, and the response echoes the event_id, content fingerprint, bound tenant, and proven producer.

Admitted infrastructure events are readable through the existing exact event route under the same tenant authority and are never projected into runtime status summaries, the lineage graph, or trade episode projections.

Against the running Flask telemetry service, a real shutdown() and startup() cycle over the same storage directory answered the replayed event with HTTP 202 duplicate=true while the restarted instance reported zero new admissions, because the durable committed receipt rather than process memory is the admission authority.

A real service instance SIGKILLed inside its durable enqueue left a reserved-not-committed claim. Retries were refused as in-flight while the lease was live, the claim was recovered by the next caller once the lease expired, and the event then reached a committed receipt — so a crash in that window neither loses the event nor strands the event_id forever.

A second telemetry service instance over the same storage directory treats an already admitted stable event ID as a duplicate, and four separate replica processes synchronising on a barrier admitted it exactly once.

Admission fails closed before any reservation and again before the commit unless the configured buffer proves durability through its own is_durable(). A deployment running the volatile memory buffer answers 503 INFRA_BUFFER_NOT_DURABLE, writes no ledger record at all, and reports infrastructure_health_buffer_durable=0 on /healthz, so no committed receipt can ever outlive the only copy of an event.

There is no production-enableable volatile bypass: the gate reads only the backend's own durability, and a test sets every PANTHEON_* telemetry environment variable found in main.py, ingest_svc.py, buffer.py, and auth.py to its most permissive value at once without changing the refusal. The injectable buffer seam used by the tests is an in-process constructor argument that buffer.create_buffer and the environment-driven service builder never reach, and injecting a volatile buffer through it still fails closed.

Against a real NATS JetStream broker (file storage, work-queue retention), an admitted event was still present in the stream after the telemetry process was SIGKILLed, and the restarted service answered the producer's replay with 202 duplicate=true — the duplicate answer is backed by an event that actually survived the crash.

A backend that stops proving durability between the enqueue and the commit is refused with the reservation released, so a degraded broker cannot convert an unsafe write into an idempotent success and the producer's retry stays admissible.

A process/broker crash matrix SIGKILLs a real ingest process in each admission window — before the durable put, after the durable put but before the commit, and after the commit — and asserts both failure modes are absent: no producer is answered accepted or duplicate for an observation that is not in durable storage, and a retry with the same stable event_id always ends with exactly one committed receipt over durable copies that are byte-identical to the original event. Four concurrent replica processes over the same broker log and ledger produce exactly one accepted admission, one durable copy, and one committed record.

A reservation that is not followed by a durable enqueue is released with an append-only, token-scoped released record, so a failed admission never blocks the producer's retry, and an owner whose lease was taken over is fenced out of both commit and release.
This task grants no broker, allocation, deployment, runtime-control, or incident-mutation authority; infrastructure health carries only an optional incident_ref string that telemetry never acts on.

readback_canonical_write_sink.containment: The Postgres write path and its ON CONFLICT (event_id) idempotency are proven unchanged by L12-TEL-001 and by the telemetry suite; this task only changes what may be admitted into the buffer, and it admits strictly less than before.
readback_canonical_write_sink.description: The bounded local readback ran without TELEMETRY_DB_DSN, so the canonical write sink behind the broker was the in-process dev sink and the batch interval was raised so the writer would not acknowledge inside the readback window. readback_canonical_write_sink.recheck_trigger: Before enabling infrastructure health in a deployed root.

reservation_lease_tuning.containment: The lease defaults to 30 seconds, far above the durable enqueue latency of the supported buffers, and a lease that is too short only causes retryable in-flight or fenced answers, never a false success or a lost event.
reservation_lease_tuning.description: TELEMETRY_INFRASTRUCTURE_HEALTH_LEASE_SECONDS must exceed the worst-case durable enqueue latency, and cross-host replicas sharing one ledger volume also share its wall-clock assumption.
reservation_lease_tuning.expiry: When telemetry replicas are deployed with a tuned lease.
reservation_lease_tuning.recheck_trigger: Before scaling telemetry beyond one host.

shared_ledger_volume.containment: Cross-replica idempotency and crash recovery were proven over a shared storage path with real processes, and the canonical Postgres writer keeps ON CONFLICT (event_id) as the final idempotency authority when replicas do not share a volume.
shared_ledger_volume.description: The durable admission ledger deduplicates across replicas only when they mount the same TELEMETRY_STORAGE_DIR or TELEMETRY_INFRASTRUCTURE_HEALTH_LEDGER path.
shared_ledger_volume.expiry: When telemetry replicas are deployed with a documented shared volume.
shared_ledger_volume.recheck_trigger: Before scaling telemetry beyond one replica.
